input.quote: 6.1 Except as provided in Section 6.2, during the term of this Agreement, the Company shall not participate in any project similar to the Site on the Internet with respect to Deerskin Products or products substantially similar to Deerskin Products (including, without limitation, the products of Wilson's House of Leather, Excelled and companies similar to Wilson's House of Leather and Excelled)
input.rationale: Section 6.1 (p0037) binds us (the Company) not to participate in any project similar to the Site with respect to Deerskin Products "or products substantially similar to Deerskin Products", including products of "companies similar to" two named retailers. That scope is open-ended rather than a named competing product, so it fails the fallback on a material term. The only carve-out (Section 6.2, p0040) is a closeout-merchandise web site; there is no permission for our internal development or for acquisitions. The restriction is also tied to a one-year term that renews automatically on each anniversary (Section 4.1, p0024), so it can run well beyond 12 months. Section 6.3 restricts HDI and benefits us, so it is not flagged. We therefore take the preferred position and delete our covenant, leaving HDI's exclusive right to the "Deerskin" branded site (and Section 6.2) untouched; the fallback narrowing is offered in the comment.

proposal.summary: Delete the non-compete covenant binding the Company in Section 6.1, leaving HDI's brand exclusivity intact.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept a restriction on the projects or products our business may pursue, so we have deleted the covenant in Section 6.1 barring us from participating in similar Internet projects for Deerskin Products or "substantially similar" products; HDI's exclusive right to the "Deerskin" branded site is preserved. If HDI needs protection, we could look at a restriction limited to a named competing product, during the term only and no more than 12 months, with carve-outs for our internal development and acquisitions.
